item.title: Penguins GM Kyle Dubas Provides Update on Ben Kindel After Medical Event on Team Flight
item.description: Penguins GM Kyle Dubas Provides Update on Ben Kindel After Medical Event on Team Flight originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Penguins placed forward Ben Kindel on injured reserve after he experienced a medical episode on a team flight. On Thursday morning, Pittsburgh president of hockey operations and general manager Kyle Dubas explained what happened during Tuesday's flight. Dubas told reporters that Kindel collapsed 10 minutes into the flight from Salt Lake City to Pittsburgh. The event was described as a "vasovagal episode," which occurs when someone faints because the body "overreacts to certain triggers," per the Mayo Clinic . The medical staff on the plane quickly attended to Kindel, who regained consciousness. The plane then made an emergency landing back in Salt Lake City, and Kindel was transported to the University of Utah Hospital. Kindel was cleared to fly back to Pittsburgh on Wednesday. "I think anyone who's been a part of any episode of that nature, you gain a deep appreciation very quickly for the way that people are trained to handle them," Dubas said. Kyle Dubas spoke to the media this morning on the status of Ben Kindel. https://t.co/YtnHDTkILm — Pittsburgh Penguins (@penguins) October 22, 2026 It is unclear what triggered the event, but Dubas said that Kindel will undergo further testing. "We will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben," Dubas said. "That's our primary goal and paramount to his future and health. ... Our hope is to get everything done, tested, back into training here in the next four days or so and then see if he can return to practice on Sunday or Monday. "I would put an asterisk on that by saying we'll see how everything goes before then." Pittsburgh will face Florida and Nashville at PPG Paints Arena on Thursday and Saturday, respectively, before a four-day break. item.title: Official Juventus team to face Rennes in Europa League
item.description: Official Juventus team to face Rennes in Europa League Juventus hosts Rennes in the Europa League, a game that offers them a chance to get back to form, and this is the team announced by Luciano Spalletti. Juventus team v Rennes The Bianconeri have struggled with their domestic duties, but there is no doubt that they are having fun in Europe and can continue to do just that. They have won two of two games in the Europa League, the second of which was away from home against Celta Vigo , so they will be filled with confidence ahead of this match. However, they were beaten at home by Lazio at the weekend, and it is the type of defeat that could weigh anyone down, so this might be a difficult spell for the Bianconeri. A Chance to Bounce Back Juve has to do better in the game, but Rennes would not make it easy for them, although their domestic form is similarly not the best so far. However, in Europe, they have not lost any of their Europa League games so far, so it will not be easy for Juve to see them off. The home crowd will expect a response, and the players know that a win is essential to restore confidence. Rennes’ unbeaten run in Europe makes them a dangerous opponent, and Juventus cannot afford to underestimate them. What Juventus Must Do The Bianconeri’s European form has been a bright spot in an otherwise difficult period, and a win against Rennes would build on that momentum. The team must show the same intensity and organisation that has served them well on the continent. Juventus’s fans will demand a much better performance than the one against Lazio, and the players must rise to the occasion. The match is an opportunity to make a statement, and the club cannot afford to let it slip. Rennes will be no pushovers, but Juventus have the quality to get a result if they play to their potential. The pressure is on, and the response must come now. The fans expect nothing less.

item.title: Roma lose Pellegrini for at least 6-8 weeks with serious injury
item.description: Roma lose Pellegrini for at least 6-8 weeks with serious injury Lorenzo Pellegrini is expected to be out of action for six to eight weeks after tests showed the Roma captain suffered a high grade lesion in the right thigh. The midfielder had pulled up during Tuesday’s Champions League victory over Slovan Bratislava , with goals from Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolò Pisilli and Donyell Malen. It was hoped that he had stopped in time before doing any significant damage, but today’s test results were far worse than predicted. Pellegrini out for two months ITALY – OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Pellegrini of AS Roma and Assane Diao of Como 1907 clash during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and AS Roma at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Sky Sport Italia report Pellegrini has sustained a high grade lesion at the site of the distal musculotendinous junction of the semitendinosus muscle in the right thigh. This kind of injury will require at least six to eight weeks on the sidelines, so Roma cannot expect the veteran back until after the next break for international duty in November. BOLOGNA, ITALY – MARCH 12: Lorenzo Pellegrini of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Round of 16 First Leg match between Bologna FC 1909 and AS Roma at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on March 12, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) It is a further blow to Gian Piero Gasperini, who is already dealing with injuries for Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné and Mile Svilar. At least Bryan Cristante made his return to the squad after more than a month out.

item.title: Stirling's 56 leads Ireland to win in Namibia
item.description: Paul Stirling scored 56 as Ireland set Namibia a target of 230 [Getty Images] First one-day international, Windhoek Ireland 229-9 (50 overs): Stirling 56 (71); Loftie-Eaton 4-36 Namibia 174 (37.5 overs): Trumpelmann 50 (43); Hoey 3-29 Ireland win by 55 runs, lead five-game series 1-0 Scorecard Ireland began their five-game one-day international series in Namibia with a comfortable 55-run win. Having lost the toss and been put in to bat, captain Paul Stirling led the way for his side with a half-century in Windhoek. Namibia never seemed likely to chase down the target of 230, although Ruben Trumpelmann's 50 off 43 balls coming in at number eight injected some life into their innings. Having scarcely played in the 50-over format in recent years, the win was Ireland's first ODI victory since May 2025. The series resumes in Windhoek on Saturday. Hoey impresses again as Stirling finds form The second of three 50-over series being used to prepare Ireland for next year's World Cup qualifiers, Gary Wilson's side were coming in off the back of a 4-0 loss to Afghanistan in August. After that comprehensive series defeat to conclude their home summer, the visitors arrived at the High Performance Oval amid questions over an onus on a settled top-six's ability to lift the run-rate in the early overs and the bowling attack's ability to take 10 wickets in the now unfamiliar format. The line-up, now under the guidance of new batting coach Ed Joyce, was boosted by Stirling's best ODI score since an 89 against Zimbabwe in February 2025. The skipper had three scores in the 20s and one of single figures against Afghanistan, but his 56 off 71 balls to open this series contained eight fours and a six to snap a streak of 17 international innings without a fifty. Stirling was eventually caught off the bowling of Nicol Loftie-Eaton, one of four wickets for the left-armer who also accounted for Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker and George Dockrell. The latter, selected ahead of Ben Calitz at number seven, took a pair of wickets at a cost of 22 runs, to draw within one of Kevin O'Brien's record of 114 for Ireland in the format. It was Gavin Hoey, however, who led the way with the ball for Ireland. Given the conditions, Wilson always seemed likely to go with two spinners in his attack, but his selection was complicated by the absence of leading seamer Mark Adair. Regardless, after some impressive performances against Afghanistan Hoey felt one of the sure starters and backed it up with figures of 3-29. In the absence of Adair, it was Jai Moondra who opened the bowling, crucially breaking Namibia's 48-run opening partnership with the wicket of Michael van Lingen. The left-armer finished with figures of 2-27 in eight overs to bounce back after a tough introduction to the format during the summer.

Her goal in the final helped to secure a 3-0 victory over Bumpy Pitch FC and the title. “I was sprinting back to recover on defense, saw Heather (O’Reilly) win the ball, and just went,” Shores told The Athletic . “I was exhausted, but I had to go. She put it on a platter for me. I had to finish it. Playing one-v-one in practice with Carli Lloyd the day after flying in from Germany? That was insane. They made us feel like equals … It’s such a fun tournament. The ball moves fast, everyone’s pressing, you sub out the second you’re tired, and fans are basically on top of the field.” In July, Shores signed with Angel City FC on a three-and-a-half-year deal, eschewing her remaining collegiate eligibility and interest from other clubs. The new acquisition was praised for her ability to “link play with passes, break lines, get into areas, and play with purpose.” Being “thrown straight into it,” she stepped into the starting lineup and made 12 appearances, registering her first professional finish in a 2-2 draw with the Washington Spirit and emulating “a sponge” to “get as much information” and “learn from people with more experience.” This season, Shores has maintained her standing and added three goals and eight assists in 26 appearances, including a brace to secure a September 2-0 win against Racing Louisville. After missing the playoffs in 2025, Angel City is a comfortable four points above the line and shortly should close out a spot. Her performances have been credited with helping to lead the resurgence, making an impact on both sides of the ball. “Honestly, I kind of got thrown straight into it,” Shores shared with the Los Angeles Daily News . “It was definitely a whirlwind coming straight from college, coming off the summer, but I’m so grateful for the opportunity … It kind of feels like a six-month head start to my first season … I’m extremely comfortable now, I really love it here. I love L.A., I love the team and the culture that we’re building here.” At the international level, Shores is a long-term member of the United States program, beginning in the Under-14 age group, and was a part of the squad that won the 2018 CONCACAF U-15 Championship. She featured with the Under-23 team several times in 2025 and clinched a 2-1 friendly victory over Germany with a “world-class finish.” Emma Hayes named her to the squad for the matches against Spain but declined to call her number in either fixture. Standing at five feet, nine inches tall, Shores is a progressive fullback, centre-back, and midfielder who puts up impressive chance creation and production numbers while always looking to play the long ball and hit crosses. She wins her duels, particularly in the air, is a reliable source of turnovers through tackles and interceptions, and often clears away danger. Her play has been characterized as “doing a lot of nuanced work for the team that maybe isn’t flashy.” Shores had the benefit of an initial half-season in the NWSL to get acclimated to the professional level before exploding in 2026, becoming one of the competition’s top creators. If she is able to hit an even higher level of production, then there is little that could keep her out of future USWNT rosters. With several major tournaments on the horizon, Emma Hayes may have added another powerful weapon to the arsenal.

item.title: Swansea City dealt major injury blow
item.description: Swansea City dealt major injury blow Swansea City will be without Ronald for up to two months after the winger suffered a hamstring injury in last weekend’s defeat to West Ham United. The Brazilian picked up the problem after being deployed at right-back against the Hammers and will now be sidelined for between six and eight weeks. “Ahead of this game the only news is Ronald felt his hamstring after the West Ham game,” head coach Vitor Matos said. “We assessed him and he’s out for about six to eight weeks. “That is the news at the moment. It’s not the most pleasant news but we will have to use the squad again.” There was more positive news elsewhere, with Filip Lissah available again after serving a one-match suspension and Stephen Eustaquio having returned from injury as a substitute against West Ham. Josh Key has also stepped up his recovery from a hamstring problem by returning to parts of team training, although Saturday’s trip to Queens Park Rangers will come too soon. “Josh did the first part of the session with us, so he’s on the right side of the rehab but he still won’t be involved this weekend,” Matos added. “Apart from that everyone is all good.”

item.title: Enes Kanter says the WNBA has an agenda against the Indiana Fever
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Enes Kanter still hasn’t gotten over his ejection at the Fever vs. Aces game. The WNBA took heat over double standards after letting A’ja Wilson off without a fine or suspension for stepping toward and confronting a fan during Game 2 against Indiana. And Enes Kanter is pointing out the contrast, as Wilson walked away untouched, while Kanter was booted from his courtside seat earlier this season after Natasha Cloud came over and confronted him. Enes Kanter claims the WNBA don’t want the Fever to succeed Enes Kanter has a known affiliation to Sophie Cunningham, having messaged her privately about the ongoing gender debate, as well as taking the same stance. And on the topic of the Indiana Fever , Kanter isn’t buying the league’s neutrality, claiming WNBA higher-ups were terrified of them going deep in the playoffs because of the off-court noise. He said on the Sage Steele Show : “So A’ja Wilson should have thrown out of the game immediately and should have been suspended the next game. I think the reason they did that obviously I don’t know if the league wants the Indiana Fever to to go deep in the playoffs because the the deeper they get the more conversation is was going to bring off the court. But look at the ratings when they’re in [clears throat] it. They’re almost double. So I feel like they it’s like a double-edged sword there.” Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark have dominated headlines this season, keeping the WNBA squarely in the culture war spotlight. Cunningham sparked massive national backlash and fan protests after speaking out against trans athletes in women’s sports, while Clark continues to transform the league’s footprint through sellout crowds and lucrative deals, including the new Caitlin 1s. Together, they’ve made the WNBA impossible to ignore on or off the court. However, their relationship with the WNBA hasn’t been the best, with Clark regularly calling out officials and Cunningham questioning the future of Cathy Engelbert before she decided to retire. item.title: Europa League line-ups: Juventus vs. Rennes
item.description: Europa League line-ups: Juventus vs. Rennes Juventus start Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade together for the first time as they try to keep the perfect Europa League start going against Rennes. It kicks off at the Allianz Juventus Stadium in Turin at 17.45 UK time (18.45 CEST). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Bournemouth-Milan and Ajax-Atalanta on the Liveblog. TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, looks on before the Serie A match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Juve have been in crisis in Serie A and are fresh off a disastrous 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, yet sit top of the Europa League table after wins over NEC Nijmegen and Celta Vigo. It remains to be seen which version of the Old Lady will turn up this evening, but Luciano Spalletti transforms the tactics by using Woltemade and Kolo Muani together for the first time, something both strikers have been publicly appealing for. This looks to be a 3-4-1-2 formation with Weston McKennie in a free role behind the strikers, Andrea Cambiaso and Zeki Celik pushed into more advanced positions. Francisco Conceicao joins the long list of absentees after a shoulder injury, with Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara, while Edon Zhegrova is not on the UEFA list. TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus runs with the ball during the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) Rennes sit sixth in Ligue 1 and have four points from two Europa League games, earning a 0-0 draw away to Sturm Graz and beating OFI Crete 2-1 with a late comeback. They too suffered defeat domestically at the weekend, a 4-3 thriller away to Paris FC decided deep into stoppages. Esteban Lepaul scored a hat-trick of penalties in that match, but he also sustained an ankle injury that forced them to end the game with 10 men, so has not made the trip to Turin. Coach Franck Haise is therefore tempted to change to a three-man defence, which is really more like five at the back, after some poor away results. There are some familiar faces, as former Lazio striker Boulaye Dia starts upfront with Mousa Al-Tamari. Midfielder Valentin Rongier has been linked with Serie A moves in the past, including to Juventus last year. ROME, ITALY – MARCH 04: Boulaye Dia of Lazio scores his team’s second goal past Marco Carnesecchi of Atalanta during the Coppa Italia match between SS Lazio and Atalanta BC at Olimpico Stadium on March 04, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Juventus vs. Rennes line-ups Juventus: Vicario; Gatti, Bremer, Kelly; Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners, Celik; McKennie; Woltemade, Kolo Muani Juventus bench: Pinsoglio, Neto, Boga, Kalulu, Alajbegovic, Lucumi, Sarr, Nico Gonzalez, Cabal, Merola Rennes: Samba; Ait Bou

item.title: Chris Russo claims Milwaukee Brewers denied his Pat Murphy interview request before World Series
item.description: Chris Russo claims Milwaukee Brewers denied his Pat Murphy interview request before World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Christopher Russo, aka Chris Russo , has always been recognized as one of Major League Baseball’s voices; however, his reputation might not be enough to secure him an interview with Milwaukee Brewers ’ manager, Pat Murphy. Following their sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers to secure their first World Series spot in more than four decades, Murphy appeared on Colin Cowherd’s Fox Sports Radio show and also joined SiriusXM alongside Jim Gray, Drew Brees, and Matthew Stafford. However, when Russo requested Murphy for an interview last week, the Brewers declined. “Five minutes later, the Brewers emailed my producer back and said, ‘Sorry, we cannot accommodate the request; Pat Murphy ’s schedule is too busy.’ What? I’m a Hall of Famer. I’m on First Take!” Russo yelled and ranted . “Not only that, Pat Murphy on Monday night did Let’s Go. No knocking Jim Gray, you know who was on? Stafford and Brees! They’re football guys for crying out loud! I’ve been doing radio for 40-something years.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Russo claimed that his producer submitted the request last week and Murphy had eight days before the start of the World Series. While Russo was willing to be flexible with his timing, the request was still denied by the Brewers. “You can’t get me, Pat Murphy, for 10 minutes when I’m on five days a week, eight days before he plays the first World Series game? I am a piece of garbage!” Russo finished. However, while Russo’s claims about his Hall of Fame and veteran status are true, it’s also the Brewers’ personal choice to have Murphy avoid an interview with him. Especially when the radio host started his rant by belittling the Brewers. “These are the Milwaukee Brewers; these aren’t the Yankees or the Dodgers,” he stated. "The Brewers emailed my producer back and said, 'Sorry, we cannot accommodate the request, Pat Murphy's schedule is too busy.' What? I'm a hall of famer. I'm on First Take!" item.title: Marc Marquez puts his chances of retiring within three years at 70%
item.description: Motorsport photo In an extensive conversation with Motorsport.com at Phillip Island, Marc Marquez puts the chances of him retiring when his next Ducati contract expires at 70%, and admits that he will do so “a free man”, regardless of whether he has won any more titles. Last year, ahead of the opening race of the season in Qatar, the Spaniard was unequivocal when asked where he saw himself in three years’ time: “Exactly where I am now: racing.” Since giving that answer in the gardens of Doha’s Ritz-Carlton hotel, events have moved at breakneck speed for the #93. He dominated the season to be crowned world champion again, six years after his previous title in 2019, only to injure his already battered right arm once more just days later in a crash in Indonesia. That fall forced him back under the knife, into yet another lengthy rehabilitation period, and, months later, with this season’s championship already underway, to come to terms with the new reality he faces on the bike, particularly at certain types of circuits. With all that behind him, Marquez gave a considerably different answer to the same question this time around, suggesting that the contract he signed with Ducati over the winter, which runs until the end of 2028, has a strong chance of being his last. Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Marc Marquez, Ducati Team “This time, it’s a little more complicated to answer that question. I don’t know exactly, but, if I had to put a figure on it, I’d say there’s a 70% chance that I’ll have retired within three years, and a 30% chance that I’ll still be racing,” Marquez said on Thursday, speaking from the garden of the house he shares with his brother Alex, a five-minute drive from Phillip Island. The 102 points he clawed back from the championship leader in just seven races, between the Italian and San Marino Grands Prix, made it abundantly clear that his ambition remained undiminished. item.title: Charles Barkley jokes about Shaq’s ‘dangerous’ Kash Patel relationship after FBI Special Agent honor
item.description: Charles Barkley jokes about Shaq’s ‘dangerous’ Kash Patel relationship after FBI Special Agent honor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . When the legendary Shaq received an FBI honor from Kash Patel , he took a shot at his Inside the NBA co-host, Charles Barkley , who returned the favor. On Inside the NBA, Barkley asked Kenny “The Jet” Smith , “Should we be standing this close to Shaq?” He elaborated, “He’s been hanging out with Kash Patel. That’s dangerous.” Charles Barkley: "Should we be standing this close to Shaq?… He's been hanging out with Kash Patel. That's dangerous." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Via: https://t.co/HRPq4bZt5X Via @ESPNNBA pic.twitter.com/DoyyEYgiqA — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 22, 2026 This made everyone, including Shaq, crack up laughing. “Diesel” put his arm around Barkley as he laughed as the program went to commercial break. It has only been a couple of days since the season started, but Inside the NBA is already delivering memorable moments. This is also Barkley’s last hoorah before he retires from broadcasting. Shaquille O’Neal was named an honorary FBI Special Agent during his graduation ceremony for Session 299 of the FBI National Academy on Thursday, Sep. 17. After receiving the honorary title, Shaq joked, “If you see Charles Barkley, arrest him.” His joke received laughter from the crowd at the ceremony. To be clear, the title is ceremonial. Barkley and Shaq have been together on Inside the NBA for years. However, their run will end after the 2026-27 season. In September 2026, he stated that he was going to go for as long as Ernie Johnson did. Now, they are both preparing to leave the show after this season. He spoke to WSFA12 News a few weeks after making his initial announcement. Barkley confirmed that he was “going to take a step back from public life” after this season. He has enjoyed his time in the spotlight, but he’s ready to move on. It’s not all bad, though. Barkley said that this season would be “more like a celebration,” since he has “had the greatest life a person could have.” We’ll have to wait and see how Inside the NBA recovers after losing Barkley and Johnson after this year. In the meantime, enjoy all of the moments they give us with Shaq and Smith. item.title: NFL has made its decision on C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s suspension appeal
item.description: The NFL has made its decision on C.J. Garnder-Johnson. The league has upheld its one-game suspension of the Buffalo Bills safety stemming from his spitting incident during Week 6’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Hearing officer Jordy Nelson, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has upheld the one-game suspension of C.J. Gardner-Johnson. — Michael Signora (@NFLfootballinfo) October 22, 2026 Given Gardner-Johnson’s on-field history of instigation and a past in-game ejection, Nelson’s decision to uphold this suspension is not majorly surprising. So Gardner-Johnson will not be available for the Bills home game against the Ravens in Week 8 on November 1. He’ll be available to return to the team, as normal on November 2. We’ll see how Sam Franklin Jr.‘s appeal goes likely in the next few days.

item.title: Mason Miller trade proposal with Dodgers makes little sense for Padres
item.description: Mason Miller trade proposal with Dodgers makes little sense for Padres originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mason Miller was a hot topic at the trade deadline, but the San Diego Padres opted to keep him in the closer role for the postseason. Miller led the National League with 38 saves and struck out 16.6 batters per nine innings in 66 appearances in 2026. It's highly plausible more teams will reach out to the Padres about Miller's services this offseason. Could the Los Angeles Dodgers be one of them? "The Dodgers don’t necessarily need Miller, but they love to acquire star players. He would provide more certainty as the closer than Edwin Diaz or left-hander Tanner Scott," FanSided's John Perrotta . Perrotta's trade proposal sends outfielder Mike Sirota, the No. 19 prospect in baseball, to the Padres for Miller. "Because of their outstanding outfield depth, the Dodgers could offer Sirota, their No. 3 prospect and No. 19 overall. "The 23-year-old would likely begin next season as the Padres’ left fielder and provide a significant upgrade over the Dustin Harris/Samad Taylor platoon," Perrotta added. In theory, this trade idea makes sense for the Padres. However, they should be looking to keep Miller and add another outfielder via free agency or the trade market. Plus, Sirota has only played 71 games at Double-A and two games at Triple-A in his minor league career. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player At 23, the right-handed hitter may require more development before making an everyday impact in the Majors. I'm also not sure that Sirota by himself is worth the next three years of Miller's contract. The flamethrower will hit the free agent market in 2030. item.title: Cesc Fabregas reflects on telling Como to 'slow down' after taking 4-0 lead against Man United
item.description: Cesc Fabregas's Como beat Manchester United 4-1 on Wednesday -Credit:Nicolò Campo, LightRocket via Getty Images Cesc Fabregas has admitted he instructed his Como squad to 'slow down' after they stormed into a 4-0 lead against Manchester United in the UEFA Champions League. The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder is at the helm of the Italian club, which savored one of the most memorable evenings in their history as they dismantled the Red Devils on Wednesday. Joshua Zirkzee netted a late consolation for United, but the result leaves Michael Carrick's position hanging by a thread . United have claimed just two victories from 11 matches across all competitions so far this season. Bruno Fernandes questions Manchester United staff's tactics after defeat to Como Ex-Liverpool boss Jürgen Klopp still grieving Diogo Jota's death in new biography -Credit:Marco Luzzani, Getty Images It could have been even more damaging for Carrick's squad, as Fabregas confessed he urged his players to ease off the accelerator after establishing a 4-0 cushion, looking to conserve their energy ahead of upcoming fixtures. "I regret the last ten minutes because I was the one who told the team to slow down the tempo because there's another match and at 4-0 we could manage things a little," said the Spaniard, as per The Mirror . "I told the players to stop running and stay in the middle and that is something I regret because I'm the first to always push them to fight until the end. "Their goal hurt me because we dropped our intensity and dropped our defensive block, but it was my fault." Carrick is now facing a battle to retain his position as United manager despite only signing a two-year deal in the summer following an impressive stint as caretaker boss. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE He took aim at his players in his post-match press conference, saying: "We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure. "It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me. "It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters. "I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

item.description: ‘The Big Fish’ — NFL Reporter Names 5-Time Pro Bowler As ‘Potential Blockbuster Target’ for Cowboys Ahead of Trade Deadline The Dallas Cowboys could make a major move to fix their struggling defense before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. After starting the 2026 season 2-4, Dallas has struggled to get opposing quarterbacks on the ground, recording just eight sacks through six games. The team’s defense also ranks second-last in PFN’s NFL Defense Impact metric, with a 69.0 grade. With the Cowboys in need of help on the defensive line, NFL reporter Jason La Canfora has identified Las Vegas Raiders star Maxx Crosby as a potential blockbuster target. Jason La Canfora Reveals Cowboys’ Potential Trade Plans Crosby remains one of the biggest names Dallas could pursue before the deadline. The five-time Pro Bowler has attracted interest because of his ability to pressure quarterbacks, and the Cowboys have reportedly shown interest in acquiring him in the past. Dallas has already shown serious interest in Crosby, with Jones acknowledging earlier this year that the Cowboys were in the mix to acquire him. Dallas has also restructured contracts to create more salary-cap flexibility, which could help the team explore a major trade if Las Vegas is willing to negotiate. However, adding a player of his caliber could give Dallas’ struggling defense a much-needed boost. Josh Sweat Could Be a More Realistic Option While Crosby would be the headline-grabbing move, La Canfora believes the Cowboys could also pursue Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat. Sweat could be a more realistic target as Dallas looks for an experienced pass rusher without necessarily making a blockbuster offer. La Canfora said NFL teams are trying to pry Sweat away from Arizona, with Jerry and Stephen Jones expected to be near the head of the list. “Josh Sweat is someone NFL teams are trying to pry at, and Jerry and Stephen Jones will be at the head of that list… the sense we’re getting from our sources is Josh Sweat could be the guy, and that’s a trade that certainly could happen well before the trade deadline,” he said. item.title: Why Troy Aikman Felt ‘Double-Crossed’ by Joe Buck Before Monday Night Football
item.description: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck - Troy Aikman and Joe Buck (Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) An explosive backstage rift between ESPN ’s Troy Aikman and Joe Buck has finally spilled into the public eye. Following weeks of reported simmering tension, more details have surfaced detailing the pregame clash between the longtime Monday Night Football partners. According to a scoop by Puck’s Dylan Byers , the boiling point occurred inside the broadcast booth at SoFi Stadium ahead of the Buffalo Bills’ 37–34 overtime victory against the Los Angeles Rams. The pair — who have shared a 24-year booth partnership — allegedly came close to physical blows after Buck confronted Aikman over his difficult behavior in recent weeks. The root of the tension comes from the behind-the-scenes contract extension talks. ESPN quietly secured Buck to a six-year, $108 million extension earlier this year, but kept the multi-year deal under wraps without offering a complementary extension to Aikman, whose five-year, $90 million contract is set to expire at the end of this season. Neither ESPN, Buck, nor mutual representatives at Creative Artists Agency (CAA) informed Aikman that Buck’s extension had actually been finalized back in May, per Puck. The secrecy left Aikman feeling completely “double-crossed,” with industry sources telling Byers that the hidden deal was an ultimate act of betrayal by Buck. The weeks of passive-aggressive tension culminated when Buck finally snapped moments before kickoff, asking Aikman if they were “really going to do this,” leading to a confrontation where Aikman accused Buck of screwing him over in the negotiations. Related Inside Coco Gauff’s Music Video Debut in Gunna’s ‘Pop It’ While the two veteran commentators were able to put on their headsets and call the game as scheduled, the revelation sheds a light on Aikman’s recent public comments regarding his impending free agency. “I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold, with the Super Bowl and all that, and where my next landing spot might be,” Aikman said during a recent radio segment on 96.7 The Ticket . With Aikman now openly preparing for ESPN to “go in a different direction,” the reported fight in the booth signals that one of sports media’s longest broadcast partnerships may be coming to an end. item.title: Green Bay Packers share Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden injury updates
item.description: The Green Bay Packers have built a three-game winning streak heading into its Week 7 matchup in the 2026 NFL season, capped by a 23-13 triumph over Dallas last weekend. Despite the team’s recent success, uncertainty surrounds the health of several key offensive players. Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden were all listed on the Packers’ injury report Wednesday after taking part in practice on a limited basis. Love revealed that back soreness has been bothering him, but he remains confident about playing in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. According to Matt Schneidman of The Athletic, Love made it clear that missing the NFC North matchup is not a possibility, easing concerns about his availability. Packers held only what they called a job-through today so practice participations are estimated, but only one DNP today. Josh Jacobs not listed so presumably he’s full go. pic.twitter.com/48UYiLmsLy — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 21, 2026 Jordan Love’s weapons Christian Watson and Matthew Golden Oct 19, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) with wide receiver Matthew Golden (0) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images For now, there appears to be little reason to worry about the availability of Watson and Golden , as neither player’s status has raised major concerns. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have become Jordan Love’s primary deep threats for Green Bay this season. Watson, 27, tops the Packers in receiving yards with 538 and has scored six touchdowns on 29 catches from 48 targets. Golden has also made an impact in his first six weeks, recording 501 yards and three touchdowns on 30 receptions despite seeing 57 targets. The 23 year old former Texas Longhorns receiver is enjoying a breakout season. Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) smiles as he runs off the field with wide receiver Christian Watson (9) after the two connected on a touchdown pass against the Los Angeles Chargers in the thrid quarter during their football game Sunday, November 19, 2023, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. Detroit’s struggles against the pass could give Green Bay a chance to put its aerial attack on full display. The Lions are surrendering 297.4 passing yards per game, the highest average in the NFL this season. The Packers won the game, 23-13. Diomande: the 150m euro player starting to show his value Diomande is a very exciting prospect in Mourinho's attacking puzzle and he is finally beginning to show why Real invested so heavily in him. Arriving from RB Leipzig after an impressive 2025–26 campaign when he recorded 12 goals and nine assists, Diomande caught Real's attention with his pace, direct dribbling and ability to beat defenders one-on-one. He has also recognised the progress being made, adding: "He has a lot to improve, but he's had a great game. He's developing." Now, Vinicius' suspension presents Diomande with an even bigger opportunity. After impressing on the left wing against Sevilla and Leipzig, he is set to have three La Liga matches without direct competition from the Brazilian, beginning with El Clasico against Barcelona on Sunday. It is arguably his biggest test since arriving at the Bernabeu, giving him the chance to prove he can deliver on the biggest stage and establish himself as more than just a promising prospect and challenge Vinicius for a regular starting spot. The question for Mourinho will be what happens when Vinicius returns, particularly as he remains available for Champions League action. If Diomande can turn his recent run of starts into consistent goals, assists and decisive performances, he could become a crucial part of Real's attack and begin to justify the enormous investment the club have made in him. Endrick: second chance to make his mark Endrick's situation is more complicated. The 20 year-old Brazilian arrived in Madrid with enormous expectations, but competition for attacking places has made consistent opportunities difficult to secure. After gaining experience during a loan spell at Lyon in the second half of the 2025-26 campaign, he has returned to a squad packed with established stars. His performance against Roma offered a reminder of what he can bring. Endrick's acceleration, direct running and willingness to attack defenders gave Real an extra dimension as they fought their way back into the match. At his best, Endrick is capable of changing the tempo of an attack. He can operate from the right, drive towards goal and threaten as a central striker. That versatility could be especially useful when Real need to change their approach during a game. His combination of pace and close control also offers a possible solution against opponents who press aggressively. Rather than relying exclusively on intricate passing, Madrid could use Endrick to carry the ball into dangerous areas and force defenders to retreat. The priority must be to give Endrick a clearly defined role and enough meaningful minutes to build his confidence. Espi: few minutes, big impact The Spanish striker is making a name for himself as one of Real's most effective impact players, showing that he could be a real weapon coming off the bench. The 21-year-old has made the most of his very limited opportunities, scoring three goals in only 37 minutes across La Liga and the Champions League, a brilliant return that has strengthened calls for him to receive more opportunities. Espi offers Real something different from their more mobile forwards: a natural centre-forward who can occupy central defenders, attack crosses and provide a focal point inside the penalty area. He is 6ft 4in tall and arrived after an 11-goal league campaign with Levante. He gives Mourinho a different tactical option when Real need to change the game. Maintaining that scoring rate over a longer period will be difficult, and Mbappe's place as the main striker limits Espi's opportunities to start. But that may be where his greatest value lies for now. He can enter games against tired defenders, bringing fresh energy into the penalty area and giving Real a different attacking option when they need to chase a result. If he continues to deliver in those crucial moments, Espi could become far more than a substitute and he could be the reliable game-changer Mourinho turns to when the pressure is highest.

Much of Washington’s struggles can be attributed to Dan Quinn’s poor game management. ​In Week 5 against the New York Giants, Washington had the ball in Giants territory in the final seconds of overtime. item.title: Lionel Messi reflects on his love for Barcelona after returning to Spain for Princess of Asturias honor
item.description: Argentinian football legend Lionel Messi poses with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo on the eve of receiving the Princess of Asturias Award for Sport, in Oviedo on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Miguel RIOPA / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Barcelona legend Lionel Messi has returned to Spain to collect The 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. The GOAT has been in Oviedo where he spoke about life at Barca and admitted it’s difficult for him to find the words to describe his time at Camp Nou. “It was a privilege to share a dressing room with Xavi, Iniesta, Puyol and so many others. We were fortunate enough to win everything, and to do it the way we did: how much we enjoyed playing, winning and achieving great things. But above all, we enjoyed our day-to-day life, the training sessions; we had a wonderful time,” he told EFE. “It is difficult to sum up in a few words. I experienced so many incredible moments and obviously hold a very, very special affection for both the city and the club.” Messi was announced as the winner of the award earlier this year and has become the first individual footballer to be given the honor by the committee. “In addition to his dazzling talent, his exceptional sporting career and his remarkable and sustained charitable work to promote access to education and healthcare for the most disadvantaged children,” a statement read. “Leo Messi, the player who has won the most titles in the history of football, has also earned the respect and admiration of everyone for his exemplary behaviour on the field and for his consistency, humility and commitment to the team game.” The award notable achievements in various fields, including Sports, Arts, Literature, Science etc, and is voted on by a jury of several members.

item.description: Barcelona team news: Youngster set to start against Real Madrid after impressive PSG display Xavi Espart is expected to retain Barcelona’s right-back spot for Sunday’s El Clasico against Real Madrid after impressing Hansi Flick with a standout performance against Paris Saint-Germain, reports Javi Miguel of AS . The 19-year-old academy graduate has reportedly convinced the Barcelona coach that he deserves to start at the Spotify Camp Nou, with Jules Kounde unlikely to be fit enough to feature from the opening whistle. Espart’s display in Paris was particularly impressive given the quality of the opposition. He helped contain Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, one of Europe’s most dangerous wingers, and capped his performance with a goal. Barcelona, therefore, are now expected to keep faith with the youngster as they prepare for another demanding test against Real Madrid. Espart’s PSG performance convinces Flick Espart has emerged as one of Barcelona’s most encouraging stories this season. Flick had already been impressed by the teenager’s contribution at left-back, where he has challenged established options Joao Cancelo and Alejandro Balde for opportunities. However, his performance on the right against PSG appears to have strengthened his case even further. Xavi Espart was impressive vs PSG. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Espart limited Kvaratskhelia’s influence and contributed at the other end, demonstrating a combination of defensive discipline and attacking confidence that is difficult to overlook. The challenge against Real Madrid will be different. With Vinicius Jr. suspended, Espart could face Yan Diomande, who presents another demanding test. Nevertheless, his display against Kvaratskhelia has given Flick reason to trust him in another high-profile fixture. Espart’s performance was all the more notable because he was managing discomfort in his quadriceps before the match. He had worked with a physiotherapist to ease the tension in the area and also took a heavy knock to his ankle during the game . Neither issue is expected to prevent him from playing on Sunday, according to the report. Kounde injury opens the door Set to start vs Real Madrid. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Kounde’s ankle sprain has further strengthened Espart’s chances of starting against Real Madrid. The immediate priority is Sunday’s Clasico , but Espart’s form could force Flick to reconsider the defensive hierarchy beyond this one match. item.title: Will Rams-Raiders be on in my area? Week 7 broadcast map, TV channel
item.description: For the first time this season, the Los Angeles Rams will play a non-prime-time game in back-to-back weeks. After facing the Arizona Cardinals last Sunday afternoon, they'll now take on the Las Vegas Raiders this coming Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. The Rams can now settle into a more regular rhythm and routine, knowing they won't be playing across the globe or in abnormal time slots like Thursday night or Monday night. The downside for fans is that the game won't be broadcast nationally in the U.S. Rather, only a select portion of the country will get Rams- Raiders on FOX this Sunday. Check the map from 506 Sports below to see if you'll have it on TV in your area. If you're in the blue, you're good to go. It'll be Chris Myers and Jonathan Vilma on the call this week after Kenny Albert and Greg Olsen had last week's game against the Cardinals. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX as the Rams try to inch closer to .500 following a 2-4 start. The Raiders, meanwhile, are looking to pull above .500, entering this game at 3-3 after starting the year 3-0. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Will Rams-Raiders be on in my area? item.title: Bengals’ Joe Burrow completely downplays JD Vance’s practice visit
item.description: Bengals’ Joe Burrow completely downplays JD Vance’s practice visit appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After receiving a surprise visit from Vice President JD Vance at practice, it didn’t appear that Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was moved at all. Speaking to the media after practice, Burrow was asked about Vance’s visit. He barely acknowledged the vice president, saying they didn’t have a chance to interact . He explained, “He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice.” Burrow elaborated by saying that he loves that football brings people together. Burrow appreciates people being interested in his job and wanting to see him practice, but again, he didn’t mention Vance in this part of his response. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow said Bengals owner Mike Brown told him at the start of practice JD Vance would be attending Burrow on the vice presidential visit to Paycor Stadium: pic.twitter.com/hAktahQopW — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 “A lot of people around. That’s what I love about what I do,” he said when asked for his thoughts on having everyone at practice. “It brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I’ve put in to come and watch greatness. That’s everybody in the locker room; that’s why we do what we do. Whether it’s on the TV, whether it’s in-person, whether it’s on the practice field, that’s what we do.” Why was JD Vance at Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ practice? Jack Gruber-USA TODAY Network Vance, an Ohio native, was making the rounds while campaigning in Cincinnati on Wednesday, Oct. 21. He headed to the Bengals’ practice after his rally to watch the action. He got to tour the locker room and shake hands with Bengals head coach Zac Taylor, even wishing the team “good luck,” according to The Enquirer. It doesn’t appear he got to interact with the team very much aside from the coach. At the very least, he didn’t have a chance to meet star quarterback Burrow. item.title: Joel Klatt says Big Ten-SEC football challenge is imminent
item.description: Edit via Liam McGuire The Big Ten and SEC run college football, but as the sport tries to chart its future, the two sides haven’t found much they could agree upon. Until now? After an exhausting period of negotiations, brinksmanship, and fan unrest, college football is moving towards a 24-team College Football Playoff. he Big Ten had been holding out against the SEC’s wishes for the expanded playoff, but a compromise seems to finally have been reached with ESPN maintaining the exclusive rights . The opinions on the move wildly vary across the spectrum with some applauding the decision to expand postseason access while others believe it could be the death knell for the sport as we know it . One of the worries about a 24-team playoff is that it will make the regular season obsolete with many of the top teams in the sport basically guaranteed passage to the engorged postseason. A very real risk exists that college football could go from having the most important, intense, and dramatic regular season to being one that is an afterthought. And when it comes to non-conference scheduling, there would seem to be little incentive for top schools to schedule tough games that would wear their team out. But according to lead Fox Sports analyst Joel Klatt, that could be rectified with a coming announcement about a scheduling agreement between the Big Ten and SEC. “There are scheduling agreements that are in place once this thing expands officially,” Klatt said on KTCK in Dallas according to Football Scoop . “The next thing that will happen almost immediately is we’re going to get scheduling agreements between the SEC and the Big Ten — top-end matchups, mid-tier matchups, low-end matchups — and we’re going to be expanding the valuable matchups in the non-conference, far surpassing what we have now.” That would certainly be good news for college football fans. The tribal warfare between the SEC and Big Ten is one of the biggest rivalries in sports. After a generation of dominance by the SEC, the Big Ten has turned the tables in recent years. And as much as fans and the media love to debate hypotheticals, a challenge series up and down the standings would finally provide some real games to discuss. Most importantly for the powers that be in college football, it could also bring about new revenue opportunities, especially if the conferences look to eschew their current deals in a series of neutral site games that could command additional money. And when it comes to college football, usually what’s best for everyone’s bank accounts is what gets done. item.title: Cardinals get bad update on Jeremiyah Love for Week 7 vs. Broncos
item.description: Cardinals get bad update on Jeremiyah Love for Week 7 vs. Broncos originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 this year and are coming off a big Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Rams . In that big win, the Cardinals were able to pull off the upset despite being without Marvin Harrison Jr. after a trade and Jeremiyah Love due to injury. While the Love injury isn't deemed to be serious, he did miss Week 6, and there is some uncertainty going forward for the Cardinals' rookie running back. Unfortunately, the latest update for Week 7 isn't good. According to CBS reporter Matt Zenitz , the Cardinals are once again expected to be without Love in Week 7 when they face the Denver Broncos . Jeremiyah Love expected to miss Week 7 for 2nd missed game in a row "The current expectation is that the Cardinals will be without standout rookie running back Jeremiyah Love this week against the Broncos, sources tell CBS Sports," Zenitz reports. After missing Week 6 due to an ankle injury, this update from Zenitz now reveals Week 7 is very much in doubt, as he's not expected to play. While the Cardinals haven't ruled Love out just yet, and they might not until game day, this report from an NFL reporter does indicate that Love is going to miss another week. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will be splitting the workload in this backfield against a Broncos defense that can be very difficult to face. But with a lackluster Broncos offense on the other side of the ball, the Cardinals should be able to stay in this game and give their running back duo a chance to carry the ball a lot on Sunday if Love is indeed out. Love has had an up-and-down rookie season so far, and recently, the ankle injury issue has really held him back from breaking out as a superstar RB like the Cardinals believe he can be. item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa president Gianni Infantino dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. item.title: Brewers Should Bench Christian Yelich Against This Rays Starting Pitcher Despite Platoon Advantage
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich Christian Yelich has been one of the Brewers' best hitters in the postseason, but manager Pat Murphy has already benched the former MVP twice against tough left-handed starters. Yelich was not in the starting lineup against Tarik Skubal or Blake Snell, but he was against Robbie Ray. Yelich had a hit against Ray, but the Brewers have a great hitter in Andrew Vaughn and feel a need to get him in the game. Even though Yelich is hitting .292 in October, Vaughn is too good to leave on the bench. So far, benching Yelich against lefties for a platoon advantage with Vaughn has worked, but the Tampa Bay Rays' top four starters are all right-handed. Is Vaughn going to stay on the bench the entire World Series and be reduced to a pinch-hitter role? It's possible, but there is one starter he should start against despite Yelich having the platoon advantage: Freddy Peralta. Peralta was a Brewer for his entire career until this year, so Yelich has only faced him once in an actual game. Yelich is 1-for-3 with a double against him. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, that was when Peralta was on the New York Mets. He's been a completely different pitcher with the Rays. Vaughn has faced Peralta 11 times in his career. He is 5-for-11 with a double and a home run. That includes eight at-bats against Peralta as a Brewer, when Peralta was an All-Star-caliber pitcher. Vaughn has been a great hitter all season, against both lefties and righties. However, Jake Bauers has been so good that he cannot be benched. Bauers is a little banged up, so the Brewers are not going to stick him in right field as they did in the regular season in order to get him, Vaughn and Yelich in the lineup together. Benching Yelich against Peralta in favor of Vaughn would look confusing on paper. However, Vaughn has great numbers against him, and there is no real starter on the Rays Vaughn would start against. If the Brewers want to get the most out of him, they should start him against Peralta. More MLB: Brewers Hitters Have Eye Popping Career Numbers Against Rays Top Three Pitchers

item.title: Browns’ Deshaun Watson’s house party after Ravens stunner even left Todd Monken surprised
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Browns’ Deshaun Watson’s house party after Ravens stunner even left Todd Monken surprised appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Deshaun Watson took the Cleveland Browns ’ biggest win of the season beyond the field. He hosted a team gathering that even caught head coach Todd Monken off guard. Following Cleveland’s dramatic 13-10 walk-off victory over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Watson welcomed teammates to his home Monday night for food, video games, and cards. The celebration came as the Browns moved into sole possession of first place in the AFC North. It gave a hard-working locker room another reason to connect . After beating the Ravens on Sunday, #Browns QB Deshaun Watson treated his teammates to a party at his house. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Watson provided food trucks and video games while the group played cards and hung out. "We've been talking about it for a while. The guys have been wanting to come by… pic.twitter.com/Yda8JBFBUg — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) October 21, 2026 “The guys have been wanting to come by the house, and I think the timing was just everything,” Watson explained. “After the game they were just like ‘party at 4’s crib,’ so I just made it happen.” Monken, however, admitted he had no advance knowledge of the gathering until shortly before his media availability. “First off, I had no idea,” the coach said, adding that someone had mentioned a possible party at another player’s home. Beyond the laughs, Monken sees value in teammates spending time together away from football. He believes those relationships can strengthen accountability when games get difficult. “The more you spend time with someone, the more you embrace them, the more you connect, the more you grow closer to loving that person, the harder it is to let them down,” Monken said. For a team built around gritty, late-game wins, that chemistry could become a meaningful advantage. Cleveland’s 2026 season has been an unlikely climb. The Browns enter Week 7 with a 4-2 slate . The offense still faces protection issues and injuries. However, the defense has helped keep Cleveland competitive. As the Browns prepare to face Tennessee, Watson’s gathering offered another sign that their growing bond may be just as important as their clutch performances. The Carolina Hurricanes are 8-2-1 in 2026-27 and again one of the NHL’s top teams despite missing their leading goal scorer from the past two seasons — but that absence could end Thursday night. The Canes activated star forward Seth Jarvis from the injured non-roster list Wednesday, putting him in position to make his season debut against the Edmonton Oilers at Rogers Place. The 24-year-old underwent shoulder surgery shortly after Carolina won its second Stanley Cup in franchise history. His initial recovery timeline was 4-6 months, meaning a return Thursday would come nearly four months after the procedure. The Hurricanes dominated the playoffs, losing just once through the first three rounds before beating the Knights in six games. Jarvis has been remarkably consistent, emerging as one of the club’s most important players over the last three seasons. The Winnipeg, Manitoba, native has recorded three consecutive 30-goal campaigns, scoring 33 times in 2023-24 and 32 in both 2024-25 and 2025-26. The No. 13 overall selection in the 2020 NHL Draft has amassed 200 points in 225 games since 2023-24, along with a plus-41 rating while averaging nearly 19 minutes of ice time. His return would provide a massive boost for a Carolina team again among the leading Stanley Cup contenders. The Canes have lost just twice in regulation through 11 games and lead the early Presidents’ Trophy race. Along with activating Jarvis, the Hurricanes recalled Skyler Brind’Amour from the American Hockey League’s Chicago Wolves and reassigned Bradly Nadeau. Brind’Amour — the son of head coach Rod — has recorded two goals and an assist in six AHL games this season. He gives Carolina another option down the middle with captain Jordan Staal sidelined. Thursday’s matchup could throw Jarvis and Brind’Amour right into the fire against a 7-1-1 Oilers team led by Connor McDavid, who has amassed a ridiculous 26 points in nine games. Puck drops at Rogers Place just past 9 p.m. ET.

The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
